title: guard PROVENANCE_HEADING drift across pack-apply/assimilate/pack-reconcile (content_integrity hashing coupling)
description: Fast-follow LOW from the TASK-142 fix-round review (2026-07-12). After TASK-142's content_integrity fix, canonicalizeSkillTextForContentHash (src/pack-apply.js) anchors the hash-line exclusion to the `## Sources & provenance (hivemind)` heading. That heading string now exists as an independent copy in src/pack-apply.js (~L28/187), src/assimilate.js (~L102, buildProvenanceBlock/PROVENANCE_HEADING), and src/pack-reconcile.js (~L28). HASHING-CORRECTNESS COUPLING: if these strings ever drift, canonicalizeSkillTextForContentHash finds no heading, skips canonicalization, and EVERY untampered skill false-mismatches at reconcile (fail-closed but wrong — legitimate installs break). The three are identical today and the round-trip e2e tests would catch drift so it can't ship silently, but there is no direct guard.\n\nFIX (pick one): (a) a single shared exported PROVENANCE_HEADING constant imported by all three modules, or (b) a fast-tier meta-test asserting the three copies are byte-equal (same pattern as the existing doc-lock/parity sensors). Prefer (a) if the import graph allows it cleanly; (b) is the minimal safety net. Low priority — reviewer classified it LOW (guarded by existing round-trip tests), non-blocking.
acceptance_criteria: The PROVENANCE_HEADING string is protected against silent cross-file drift by EITHER a single shared exported constant imported by src/pack-apply.js, src/assimilate.js, and src/pack-reconcile.js, OR a fast-tier meta-test that fails red if any of the three copies diverges.
If a meta-test route: it is non-vacuous (temporarily changing one copy makes it fail).
If a shared-constant route: content_integrity round-trip + reconcile e2e stay green (no behavior change), and the hashing anchor still resolves correctly.
Per-ticket gate green; npm test + affected e2e (assimilate, pack-apply, pack-reconcile). dist rebuilt only if an affected bundle changed.
